post.summary: Records a visit that has already happened. Rule 109.

get.summary:
The re-inspection worklist: badged listings nobody has visited inside the
interval, longest overdue first. A query rather than a sweep, because a WHERE
clause is right without having had to run.

parameters.description: The moment the worklist is built. On the query so a test can move it.

post.summary:

and refused for an admin who does not make visits.

Takes the badge off, with a reason. Any admin, because a claim being withdrawn
should not wait for the one person who makes visits.

parameters.description:
Optional. Omitted, the queue is every listing in the product, which is what
the admin panel opens on before a tab is chosen.

get.summary: One listing with its photos, facilities, verification checks and owner.

post.summary:
Takes a published listing off the site, with a note saying why. Rule 122: §5 had
ten admin listing endpoints and none of them set `Unpublished`, so the
status existed in the enumeration and could never be reached.
Publishes a listing. Refused until all four verification checks have passed.
Rejects a listing. The note is required and is sent to the owner.
Sends a listing back to its owner. The note is the message they read.
Records one verification check, replacing any earlier verdict of the same type.

parameters.description:
Content or Availability. The split is the whole point of two queues: an
availability row is worked in a batch in seconds, and putting it behind a
field-by-field review is what makes owners stop confirming.

recorded and the listing is left where it is.

point of an admin user list — an account that has been switched off is exactly
the one somebody is looking for.

parameters.description: Optional. Matches a name or an email address.

permanent and left an account no route back after whatever caused it was
resolved.

Rotates a refresh token and issues a new access token.

Sets a new password using the token from the reset email, and ends every other session.

one that is already open. Rule 43 makes the second case ordinary rather than an
error, so it answers 200 where a new thread answers 201.

emailed to them if they are not — rule 105.

Marks everything the caller did not send as read, and answers with how many.
Rule 104: a thread with nothing unread is a success, not a refusal.

model binding, which rejects an empty value before the request reaches the

what makes an ownerId in the query string harmless: it is overwritten before
the query reaches a handler.

put.summary:
Edits a listing. On a published one this creates a revision and leaves the
live listing exactly as it was; on a draft it writes the change straight in.

post.summary:

after the first visit the team goes on its own schedule, and no response here
or anywhere else ever names a date that has not happened yet.
Sends a draft for review. This is the only path to PendingReview.

patch.summary:
Confirms how many beds are free. Sending the count the listing already shows
is a confirmation rather than a no-op: it is what keeps the listing off the
stale list.

post.summary: Adds one photo to a listing and generates its thumbnail.

delete.summary: Removes one photo from a listing, along with its stored files.

patch.summary: Sets the gallery order. The body must name every photo the listing will hold, exactly once.

parameters.name: OwnerId

university is comparing on the wrong axis, so the landmark carries over
from the search the shortlist came from.

rating and the count. Rule 41: a review that no admin has approved is not here,
and rule 95 keeps every one of them to a display name.
The public gallery of one published listing, in order.

Writes a review of a listing the author has completed a visit to. It is
created Pending and is invisible until an admin approves it: rule 41.

the listing, because a review depends on this and an owner alone would hold a

Withdraws a request. Rule 91: the seeker who made it, and nobody else.

AdminUserDto.description:
One account in full, and **the only shape in the product that carries a phone
number or a CNIC.**
            
This is the single exception rule 33 names, and it exists for one reason: an admin
recording the `OwnerIdentity` verification check is being asked to confirm an
identity, and rule 33 as originally written asked them to confirm it without being
shown it. The exception is deliberately narrow — this endpoint, Admin-only, and the
CNIC only for an owner because only an owner has one. Nothing changes about logging
or caching: §4.2 forbids a CNIC in a log line and the admin area is not cached.

AdminUserSummaryDto.description:
One account on the admin's user list.
            
Rule 117: **no CNIC and no phone number here.** A page of fifty accounts is fifty
identity numbers on one screen, in one screenshot and in one browser cache, for a
question the list is not being asked. The detail shape carries them; this does not,
and it is a separate type rather than a filtered version of one so that nothing can
widen it by accident.

distanceKm.description:
Straight-line kilometres from the landmark the search named, to one decimal.
Null when no landmark was named — an absent distance, not a distance of zero.

savedAt.description: When it went onto the shortlist. The list is ordered by this, newest first.

SavedListingDto.description:
A listing on someone's shortlist: the public card plus the moment they saved it.
Inheriting the public card is the safe direction — a card gains nothing private
by being read by the person who saved it, and rule 87 keeps the list to listings
that are still published anyway.

active.description: Set by the controller from which of the two endpoints was called.

SetAccountActiveCommand.description:
Rules 118 to 121. Two endpoints, one command: deactivating and reactivating differ
only in the value they write, and the three rules in front of both of them are the
same three rules.
            
§5 listed only the deactivation, which made an admin's misclick permanent and left
an account no route back even after whatever caused it was resolved.

seekerId.description: Set from the token by the controller, never from the request body.

adminId.description: Set from the token by the controller.

adminNote.description: Required. Rule 122, for the same reason rule 26 requires one.

UnpublishListingCommand.description:
Rule 122. §5 had ten admin listing endpoints and none of them set
`Unpublished`, so the status existed in the enumeration and was unreachable in
the product — a listing could never leave the public site through the API at all.
Phase 6 recorded the gap and deliberately did not close it, because upholding a
report is not the same decision as taking a listing down.

latitude.description: Nullable for the same reason as on the create command: 0.0 is a real coordinate.

longitude.description: Nullable for the same reason as RoomRaah.Application.Features.Properties.Commands.UpdatePropertyCommand.Latitude.

isEmailVerified.description: False until the emailed code has been verified.

UserSummaryDto.description:
The signed-in person's own account summary. Never used in a public response.
A phone number is deliberately absent: no DTO in this product carries one.

evidenceDate.description: The date of the evidence the admin looked at, if there was one.

note.description: What the admin wrote, if anything.

recordedAt.description: When the verdict was last recorded.

ownerResponseNote.description: What the owner wrote back. Required on a decline: rule 89.

createdAt.description: When the request was made. Both lists are ordered by this.

VisitRequestDto.description:
A visit request as both sides of it see it. Rule 93: the seeker is named by
display name, and the owner is not named at all — there is nothing here to reach
either of them with off the site, which is the whole reason visit requests exist.
